title: OM scalable crossover profiling
objective: Profile scalable higher-order OM workloads and source-transparently accelerate the exact polynomial and MaxMin loops enough to establish a measured crossover boundary without changing public selection

oracles: SageMath/PARI exact maximal-order discriminant and index

handoff.summary: Checkpoint replaces exponential monic-candidate enumeration with deterministic squarefree, distinct-degree, and Cantor-Zassenhaus modular factorization. It adds a same-source packed IntegerBuffer kernel for exact triangular-lattice closure, skips redundant products already in the equation order, and preserves a dynamic CPython fallback. The degree-32 bad-generator p=7 tree now builds in milliseconds; because exhaustive MaxMin evidence exceeds its bound, the independently valid lattice remains an inspectable incomplete candidate and cannot reach LocalOrderResult complete.
risks: Equal-degree splitting remains deterministically bounded and can still return an explicit resource error on adversarial candidates.
The degree-32 p=7 candidate has valid closure/index/type evidence but deliberately remains incomplete until scalable independent MaxMin evidence is available.
Full bad-generator index factorization exceeded the bounded oracle timeout and belongs to discriminant-component orchestration rather than this local OM lane.
next_steps: Measure warmed direct PARI nfbasis and pinned Hecke maximal_order at degrees 32 and 48 with bounded processes.
Profile and source-transparently compile the remaining type-tree and numerator-table loops on the degree-48 crossover candidate.
Coordinate the v429 exact-polynomial local candidate boundary with nf_timeout_cluster without editing its timeout or engine paths.
